revisit_notes: Lambert validated to 5.2e-05 km/s vs Curtis Example 5.2 (analytic reference) before any porkchop cell was trusted -- the higher-fidelity verification pattern borrowed from trajectory-bot.

Near-Delta-theta=pi cells (the exact 180-deg minimum-energy geometry) are SKIPPED as ill-posed (Lambert plane-singularity). The true minimum sits at ~180 deg, so the reported minimum is a slight UPPER bound on the real min-energy v_inf -- it can only be <= the hand 5.44, never spuriously below. This is the honest direction for H1.

Ephemeris is real Horizons but the porkchop uses grid points directly (no interpolation) since Saturn and Earth grids are 7d-aligned -- no interpolation error. Saturn's real 9.07-10.02 AU range (its true eccentricity) is captured.

H3's Titan cap is a magnitude bound (aligned vinf_T + v_Titan), NOT a full Saturn-frame tour. It reproduces R186 at vinf_T=3 but shows the revocation is conditional on vinf_T; a real Saturn-system Titan-tour optimizer (trajectory-bot's heliocentric tour search re-hosted in a Saturn frame) is the follow-on that would settle whether a high-vinf_T tour re-opens the lever.
Single-revolution Lambert only; long-way/multi-rev transfers not swept (min-energy Saturn->Earth is a ~6 yr single-rev short-way, well inside grid).

verdict.summary: Real JPL-ephemeris confirms the hand-derived Saturn-departure anchor: the Lambert porkchop minimum departure v_inf is 5.26 km/s (ToF 6.5 yr), bracketing the hand vis-viva 5.44 km/s and validating 6.21 as a realizable faster-transfer value -- retiring design-axes/04's 'vis-viva-default anchoring' methodology weakness for this anchor with a real-ephemeris backing (Lambert cross-validated to 5e-05 km/s vs Curtis Ex 5.2). The reactor floor is unmoved (153 kWe, inside 155-175). The one new finding is on H3: trajectory-bot's Titan constants reproduce R186's ~3.3 km/s Titan pump cap at the natural capture-orbit vinf_T~3, but the cap SCALES with vinf_T and reaches the 5.44 requirement at vinf_T>=4.01 km/s -- so R186's Titan-lever revocation holds at nominal parameters but is CONDITIONAL on the arrival-orbit vinf_T, a nuance the magnitude-bound-only R186 did not quantify. It does not move the reactor floor (the departure burn supplies v_inf regardless) but re-opens a design question: does a patient high-vinf_T Titan tour partially re-open the lever? That needs a Saturn-frame tour optimizer (named follow-on).
